# OSS KB Update Proposal: Maven `org.yaml:snakeyaml`

---

## Why Add

SnakeYAML is one of the most widely depended-upon YAML parsing libraries in the Java/JVM ecosystem. It is a transitive dependency of Spring Boot, Hibernate, Dropwizard, Apache Camel, and many other major frameworks. Eight publicly documented vulnerabilities (all with CVE aliases and GHSA records) span from 2017 through 2022, covering both denial-of-service and remote code execution attack surfaces. Despite this significant exposure, no KB page currently exists. Adding a page provides immediate value to any organisation scanning Maven dependency trees.

---

## Vulnerability Classes

| Class | CVEs / GHSAs | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| **Denial of Service – Uncontrolled Resource Consumption** | CVE-2022-25857 (GHSA-3mc7-4q67-w48m) | Missing nested-depth limit for collections allows crafted YAML to exhaust memory. |
| **Denial of Service – Stack Overflow (Out-of-bounds Write)** | CVE-2022-38749 (GHSA-c4r9-r8fh-9vj2), CVE-2022-38750 (GHSA-hhhw-99gj-p3c3), CVE-2022-38751 (GHSA-98wm-3w3q-mw94), CVE-2022-38752 (GHSA-9w3m-gqgf-c4p9) | Deeply nested or recursive YAML structures trigger `StackOverflowError`, crashing the JVM. All four originate from OSS-Fuzz findings (issues 47024, 47027, 47039, 47081). |
| **Entity / Alias Expansion (Billion-Laughs variant)** | CVE-2017-18640 (GHSA-rvwf-54qp-4r6v) | The YAML Alias feature allows exponential entity expansion during `load()`, analogous to XML bomb attacks. |
| **Unsafe Deserialization – Remote Code Execution** | CVE-2022-1471 (GHSA-mjmj-j48q-9wg2) | `Constructor` (and by inheritance any non-`SafeConstructor` loader) deserialises arbitrary Java types from YAML input. An attacker can chain gadget classes to achieve RCE, even when a target data class is specified, because type checks occur only *after* the malicious payload has already been instantiated. |

---

## Fixed-Version Narrative

| Version | What it resolves |
|---|---|
| **1.26** | Fixes CVE-2017-18640 – alias/entity expansion DoS. |
| **1.31** | Fixes CVE-2022-25857 (nested-depth limit), CVE-2022-38749, CVE-2022-38750, CVE-2022-38751 (stack-overflow DoS family). |
| **1.32** | Fixes CVE-2022-38752 (additional stack-overflow variant found by OSS-Fuzz 47081). |
| **2.0** | Fixes CVE-2022-1471 – the critical RCE via `Constructor` deserialization. In SnakeYAML 2.0 the default `Yaml()` constructor was changed to use `SafeConstructor`, which refuses arbitrary type instantiation. This is a **breaking API change**; code that previously relied on `new Yaml(new Constructor(...))` to deserialise application-specific types must be explicitly updated. |
| **2.6** (current latest) | Contains all above fixes. No additional publicly disclosed CVEs between 2.0 and 2.6 as of the evidence gathered. |

**Recommended minimum version: 2.0** to cover all known vulnerabilities, especially the RCE. For DoS-only coverage without the 2.x API break, **1.33+** addresses all stack-overflow and expansion issues, but leaves the RCE (CVE-2022-1471) unpatched.

---

## Caveats / Open Questions

1. **API breakage at 2.0:** The shift to `SafeConstructor` as default is intentionally breaking. Projects upgrading from 1.x must audit every `Yaml` instantiation site; blindly re-enabling `Constructor` re-introduces CVE-2022-1471.
2. **Transitive dependency lag:** Many frameworks (e.g., older Spring Boot 2.x trains) still ship SnakeYAML 1.x as a managed dependency. A KB page should note that overriding the managed version may require integration testing.
3. **"Out-of-bounds Write" labelling:** GitHub/NVD classify the stack-overflow CVEs under CWE-787 (Out-of-bounds Write). The actual impact is JVM crash via `StackOverflowError`; no memory corruption or code execution has been demonstrated for
